background_definition.rule: 1996 household income at or below its weighted percentile cutoff; ties kept together
background_definition.reference_population: Selected panel, birth years 1980-1984 pooled, each respondent counted once

literature_motivation.citation: Chetty, Raj, David J. Deming, and John N. Friedman (2026). Diversifying Society's Leaders? The Determinants and Causal Effects of Admission to Highly Selective Private Colleges. Quarterly Journal of Economics 141(1): 51-145.
literature_motivation.location: Section 6.1, p. 43, and Table V, row 7, in the August 2025 author version
literature_motivation.use_in_source: The need-affirmative admissions counterfactual gives the bottom parental-income quintile the largest boost, following Chetty et al. (2020). This is not the source paper's earnings-regression specification.
literature_motivation.source_income_measure: Parental household income averaged over child ages 12-17, ranked against parents of children in the same national birth cohort; negative parental income is excluded.
literature_motivation.adaptation: Single-year 1996 household income in the selected NLSY97 panel, pooling birth years 1980-1984 with custom person weights. Genuine negative baseline income is retained. These are sample-relative ranks, not national birth-cohort ranks.
literature_motivation.foundational_reference: Chetty, Friedman, Saez, Turner, and Yagan (2020). Income Segregation and Intergenerational Mobility Across Colleges in the United States. Quarterly Journal of Economics 135(3): 1567-1633. https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjaa005

labels.0: No high-school diploma or GED only

variables.female: 1 for sex code 2; 0 for sex code 1
variables.college: 1 for highest-degree codes 4-7 by the 2015 interview; otherwise 0
variables.age: Earnings calendar year minus birth year (year-end age)
variables.custom_weight: Stored custom weight / 100 (two implied decimal places)
variables.regression_weight: Custom weight divided by the person-level sample mean
variables.household_net_worth_2025: 1997 household net worth times CPI_2025 / CPI_1997
variables.low_background: 1996 household income at or below its weighted percentile cutoff; ties kept together

caveats: The 20th-percentile income-only default is motivated by the literature, selected before estimating this revised model. It is not preregistered; earlier joint income/wealth cutoffs were explored.
The cutoff is sample-relative, based on one year of household income; it does not reproduce national birth-cohort ranks of multiyear parental income.
The comparison group is all households above the income cutoff, not a uniformly wealthy group. Net worth does not determine the indicator.
The existing panel still requires observed baseline net worth for comparability with earlier analyses; this revision does not broaden the sample.

The sample includes screening-confirmed zero wage amounts and requires usable wage amounts in all three years. Unresolved skips and other missing amounts remain excluded. Zero wages do not imply zero self-employment income or nonemployment.
Custom weights belong to the selected sample. New sample membership requires compatible weights and renewed sample validation.
ASVAB_MATH_VERBAL_SCORE_PCT already normalizes within three-month birth groups; division by 1000 restores stored units.
Highest degree is fixed at the 2015 interview. High-school diploma includes some college without a higher completed degree; it does not identify never-attenders.
Codes 0-1 combine no high-school diploma and GED only; codes 5-7 combine master's, doctoral and professional degrees. These within-category differences remain pooled.
The 2025 CPI mean uses 11 supplied months: October is absent; no month is imputed.
